title: Terry Fox: Marathon of Hope
dek: The young runner who turned an amputated leg and an unfinished road into a living cancer-research movement.
mortality_event: Diagnosed with osteosarcoma at 18, Terry Fox lost his right leg, ran the 1980 Marathon of Hope across Canada, and stopped near Thunder Bay after cancer spread to his lungs before his death in 1981.
citation_passage: Terry Fox (1958–1981) was a Canadian runner who made cancer research the purpose of his Marathon of Hope. After bone cancer led to the amputation of a leg at eighteen, his experience of other patients' suffering prompted him to plan a run across Canada. He began on April 12, 1980, at the Atlantic Ocean and ran close to a marathon each day. Cancer in his lungs forced him to stop near Thunder Bay, Ontario, on September 1, after 143 days and 5,373 kilometres. Fox died on June 28, 1981, aged twenty-two. The annual Terry Fox Run continued his fundraising effort after his death. This seven-page biographical comic follows the connection between his illness, the unfinished journey, and the cancer-research movement that carried his work forward.
